chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him saying: 'A man commits a sin, and Allah enters him into Paradise because of it.' I said: 'Does Allah enter him into Paradise because of the sin?' He said: 'Yes. He commits a sin, so he does not cease to be fearful of it, hating his own self, so Allah shows mercy on him and enters him into Paradise.'
ai.seo_question: How can a sin lead to Paradise in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia concept of 'good consequences of bad deeds' (hasanāt al-dhunūb), where the spiritual benefit arises not from the sin itself, but from the resulting humility and fear of God (khawf) that prevents arrogance. The Imam clarifies that the sin acts as a catalyst for self-reproach (muqātāt al-nafs), which purifies the believer and earns divine mercy, ultimately leading to Paradise.
